text:
maria-support: FYI customer AcmePayments hit 401s right after our scheduled API key rotation at 04:00 UTC in eu-west. They say ~30% of requests failing, others fine. They rotated keys via Vault. Repro steps + snippet below. Can SRE pick this up?

jamal-sre: looking. Do we have correlation ids or sample request?

maria-support: sent sample curl and X-Request-ID header: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live:xxxx' -H 'X-Request-ID: rq_9b3f' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` -> 401 `{\"error\":\"invalid_api_key\"}`. Happens on their internal worker pool only.

kyle-support: customer says some workers were restarted after rotation and recovered, others still 401. They run on-prem behind an ssh-proxy sidecar.

jamal-sre: first guess: env var shadowing or sidecar caching old key. Did Vault agent update the file at /etc/secrets/apikey?

maria-support: they attached agent logs, see lines: `2026-03-16T04:00:12 vault-agent: wrote /etc/secrets/apikey (version 202603160400)` then later `ssh-proxy[pid]: loaded creds from /run/sidecar/creds`

rachel-eng: hmm sidecar is reading from a different mount path (`/run/sidecar/creds`) not the Vault file. If process didn't restart it won't pick up the new file.

liam-devex: quick checklist: 1) which process reads env var vs file; 2) is there a symlink drift between /etc/secrets and /run/sidecar; 3) Vault rewrap status (KMS).

ops-oncall: checked KMS logs — rewrap completed, no errors. Vault shows key version incremented. But there are a handful of nodes with older agent leases still present: `lease_id=secret/creds/worker-42 ttl=300` and agent didn't renew on node reboot.

jamal-sre: can customer run `ls -l /run/sidecar/creds && cat /run/sidecar/creds/apikey` on one failing worker? We need to confirm value mismatch.

maria-support: they ran it and returned truncated value (masked): `/run/sidecar/creds/apikey -> sk_live:OLDxxx` while /etc/secrets/apikey shows `sk_live:NEWyyy`. So shadowing confirmed.

rachel-eng: root cause likely: sidecar reads creds from a tmpfs path populated by the ssh-proxy at container start. Our Vault-agent wrote to the canonical path but didn't trigger the sidecar refresh. We have two mitigations: 1) instruct customer to restart the ssh-proxy sidecar (fast) or 2) add a small script to watch for file changes and SIGHUP the sidecar.

jamal-sre: agreed. Could also update rotation runbook to `post-hook: systemctl kill -s HUP ssh-proxy` on affected deployments. For on-prem we should be conservative.

kyle-support: customer performed restart of ssh-proxy on two failing nodes and reports requests now 200. They asked for a root cause summary for their incident report.

liam-devex: for the report include: Vault write occurred, KMS rewrap ok, mismatch due to sidecar tmpfs population only at start, some nodes not restarted so kept old creds. Recommend: change sidecar to read canonical path or implement inotify refresh, and update runbook to include sidecar refresh post-rotate.

ops-oncall: note — we should also surface a warning in Console for Private/VPC rotations that mentions sidecar/tmpfs patterns if detected (heuristic: agent writes to canonical path but container process reads from ephemeral mount).

maria-support: customer satisfied, asked for timeline of fix. I'll PR runbook changes and follow up. :white_check_mark:

vault-agent-bot: Vault write: path=secret/data/apikeys/acmepayment version=45 actor=maria-support request_id=vlt_abc123

jamal-sre: leaving a TODO: add a diagnostic check to health-checker that compares `/etc/secrets/apikey` vs `/run/sidecar/creds/apikey` on startup and report drift in our telemetry.

maria-support: thanks all — closing thread after I attach summary to ticket #5421.
